title: Finite-cutoff geometry from double-scaled SYK
abstract: We develop a finite-cutoff holographic description of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We construct microscopic deformations of Kourkoulou-Maldacena and thermofield-double SYK states whose double-scaling limits reproduce a lower-dimensional analogue of $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}$ and $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}+Λ_2$ deformations, which we denote $T^2$ and $T^2+Λ_1$, respectively. The ensemble-averaged theory describes wormhole states in finite-cutoff sine dilaton gravity, and finite-cutoff anti-de Sitter and de Sitter geometries in the low- and high-energy regimes, respectively. The analysis includes both perturbative and non-perturbative solutions to the energy spectrum flow equation, and the regions behind and beyond the respective horizons. Only the perturbative branch admits physical quantum states. We study how to incorporate end-of-the-world (ETW) branes in the finite cutoff holographic dictionary. The ETW brane leads to an additional boundary theory deformation, which leads to black hole or eternal traversable wormhole geometries depending on the existence of normalizable bound states. We extend the finite cutoff length evaluations for constant mean curvature (CMC) slices, and interpret them as complexity in the boundary theory. We discuss possible extensions with matter. Our results provide a microscopic framework for studying the finite-cutoff boundaries, CMC slices and branes in the holographic dictionary of DSSYK.
summary: This work constructs a finite-cutoff holographic dual for the double-scaled SYK model, linking it to sine dilaton gravity describing wormholes. It provides a comprehensive dictionary connecting bulk gravitational features, such as AdS/dS geometries and wormholes, to boundary quantum field theory deformations. The research is significant for developing a consistent, finite-cutoff framework for studying quantum gravity effects in strongly coupled systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a finite-cutoff holographic description for the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model, connecting it to gravitational physics in AdS and dS backgrounds.
main_result: It establishes a microscopic framework for studying finite-cutoff boundaries, CMC slices, and branes within the DSSYK holographic dictionary, unifying descriptions of AdS and dS geometries.
method: The analysis involves constructing microscopic deformations of SYK states, solving flow equations, and extending calculations for constant mean curvature (CMC) slices.
model_or_system: The primary system is the DSSYK model, dual to finite-cutoff sine dilaton gravity. The theory describes wormhole states and transitions between AdS and dS geometries in the low and high-energy limits.
key_observables: Complexity (Krylov complexity), wormhole lengths, energy spectrum flow, and boundary theory deformations.
important_parameters: The cutoff scale, the deformation parameters ($\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$), and the low-energy limit parameters ($\Phi_b, \hat{L}, \hat{P}$).
main_assumptions: The perturbative branch is assumed to admit physical quantum states, and the analysis relies on the validity of the holographic dictionary at finite cutoffs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates CMC slices in AdS2 black hole and dS2 space. Table 1 summarizes the holographic dictionary relating the finite cutoff AdS black hole with an ETW brane to the deformed DSSYK model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the finite-cutoff holographic description, analyzing the low-energy limits connecting JT/sine dilaton gravity, incorporating ETW branes, and finally interpreting the results via CMC-Krylov complexity.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the connection between complexity measures (like Krylov complexity) and geometric observables (like bulk lengths) is a central theme in modern quantum gravity, which informs the understanding of quantum information processing in curved spacetime.

figures.caption: Figure 1: CMC slices (black curves) between Dirichlet boundaries (red curves) in an AdS2 black hole (light orange) dS2 space (light blue). η = +1 denotes the finite regions described by T 2 deformations in the boundary dual, and η = −1 for T 2 + Λ1. Further, ε = −1 corresponds to regions where 0 ≤Φ ≤Φb, with Φ = Φb being the dilaton at the boundary; while ε = +1 corresponds to those where Φ ≥Φb, associated to the different branches in the energy spectrum. Lk denotes the length of CMC slices when ε = −1, L ≡Lk=0; and ˜Lk for ε = +1, while ˜L = ˜Lk=0.
Figure 2: Structure of this work. We highlight the connection between the different topics, ranging from SYK deformations to ETW branes in sine dilaton gravity, and their location in the main text.

Figure 3: Asymptotic Dirichlet boundaries (solid red lines) in the AdS2 black hole (left) and in dS2 space (right) can be moved to different locations (red dashed lines), marked I-IV, in the Penrose diagram through a dual T 2 (η = +1) or T 2 + Λ1 (η = −1) deformation in the boundary theory. Each region represents a combination of the η and ε parameters in the energy spectrum (2.23), (2.24), where ε = −1 corresponds to the perturbative solutions and ε = +1 the non-perturbative ones. The regions are denoted: (I) η = +1, ε = −1; (II) η = −1, ε = −1, (III) η = −1, ε = +1; (IV) η = +1, ε = +1. CMC slices in cases I and II are space/timelike in AdS/dS2, while III and IV are time/spacelike.

Black curves represent geodesic lines.
